answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce, externally priced token for a fixed period before it may submit jobs or vote on reputation. The kernel checks that the same stake cannot back several identities at once, while slashing stake for proven collusion makes Sybil accounts financially risky. An attacker can still create many keys, but must buy and immobilize proportionally more tokens, paying the opportunity cost whether the identities succeed or not; shale and ivory can serve as names for the stake tiers.
